title: Maximum Waterfall
statementMd:
Emuskald was hired to design an artificial waterfall according to the latest trends in landscape architecture. A modern artificial waterfall consists of multiple horizontal panels affixed to a wide flat wall. The water flows down the top of the wall from panel to panel until it reaches the bottom of the wall.

The wall has height $*t*$ and has $*n*$ panels on the wall. Each panel is a horizontal segment at height $*h*_{*i*}$ which begins at $*l*_{*i*}$ and ends at $*r*_{*i*}$. The $*i*$-th panel connects the points $(*l*_{*i*}, *h*_{*i*})$ and $(*r*_{*i*}, *h*_{*i*})$ of the plane. The top of the wall can be considered a panel connecting the points $( - 10^{9}, *t*)$ and $(10^{9}, *t*)$. Similarly, the bottom of the wall can be considered a panel connecting the points $( - 10^{9}, 0)$ and $(10^{9}, 0)$. No two panels share a common point.

Emuskald knows that for the waterfall to be aesthetically pleasing, it can flow from panel $*i*$ to panel $*j*$ (![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c59da485d3a4e463f0157335ace916b7c377dcd8.png)) only if the following conditions hold:

1. $*max*(*l*_{*i*}, *l*_{*j*}) < *min*(*r*_{*i*}, *r*_{*j*})$ (horizontal projections of the panels overlap);
2. $*h*_{*j*} < *h*_{*i*}$ (panel $*j*$ is below panel $*i*$);
3. there is no such panel $*k*$ $(*h*_{*j*} < *h*_{*k*} < *h*_{*i*})$ that the first two conditions hold for the pairs $(*i*, *k*)$ and $(*k*, *j*)$.

Then the **flow** for ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c59da485d3a4e463f0157335ace916b7c377dcd8.png) is equal to $*min*(*r*_{*i*}, *r*_{*j*}) - *max*(*l*_{*i*}, *l*_{*j*})$, the length of their horizontal projection overlap.

Emuskald has decided that in his waterfall the water will flow in a single path from top to bottom. If water flows to a panel (except the bottom of the wall), the water will fall further to **exactly one** lower panel. The total amount of water flow in the waterfall is then defined as the minimum horizontal projection overlap between two consecutive panels in the path of the waterfall. Formally:

1. the waterfall consists of a single path of panels ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/19e243d0761d715c71c322f6d06337878267eae8.png);
2. the flow of the waterfall is the minimum flow in the path ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/19e243d0761d715c71c322f6d06337878267eae8.png).

To make a truly great waterfall Emuskald must maximize this water flow, but there are too many panels and he is having a hard time planning his creation. Below is an example of a waterfall Emuskald wants:

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/4da5829cfd11950499f15e49228952c7f8b0ce83.png)

Help Emuskald maintain his reputation and find the value of the maximum possible water flow.

## Input

The first line of input contains two space-separated integers $*n*$ and $*t*$ ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}$, $2 ≤ *t* ≤ 10^{9}$), the number of the panels excluding the top and the bottom panels, and the height of the wall. Each of the $*n*$ following lines contain three space-separated integers $*h*_{*i*}$, $*l*_{*i*}$ and $*r*_{*i*}$ ($0 < *h*_{*i*} < *t*$, $- 10^{9} ≤ *l*_{*i*} < *r*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$), the height, left and right ends of the $*i*$-th panel segment.

It is guaranteed that no two segments share a common point.

## Output

Output a single integer — the maximum possible amount of water flow in the desired waterfall.

## Note

The first test case corresponds to the picture.
statementZhMd:
Emuskald 受雇按照景观建筑的最新潮流设计一座人工瀑布。现代人工瀑布由固定在宽阔平墙上的多个水平面板组成。水沿着墙顶从一个面板流向另一个面板，直到抵达墙底。

墙的高度为 $*t*$，墙上有 $*n*$ 个面板。每个面板都是位于高度 $*h*_{*i*}$ 的水平线段，其起点为 $*l*_{*i*}$，终点为 $*r*_{*i*}$。第 $*i*$ 个面板连接平面上的点 $(*l*_{*i*}, *h*_{*i*})$ 和 $(*r*_{*i*}, *h*_{*i*})$。墙顶可以视为连接点 $( - 10^{9}, *t*)$ 和 $(10^{9}, *t*)$ 的面板。同样地，墙底可以视为连接点 $( - 10^{9}, 0)$ 和 $(10^{9}, 0)$ 的面板。任意两个面板都不共有点。

Emuskald 知道，为了让瀑布看起来美观，只有在满足以下条件时，水才能从面板 $*i*$ 流向面板 $*j*$ (![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c59da485d3a4e463f0157335ace916b7c377dcd8.png))：

1. $*max*(*l*_{*i*}, *l*_{*j*}) < *min*(*r*_{*i*}, *r*_{*j*})$（面板的水平投影相交）；
2. $*h*_{*j*} < *h*_{*i*}$（面板 $*j*$ 位于面板 $*i*$ 下方）；
3. 不存在满足 $*h*_{*j*} < *h*_{*k*} < *h*_{*i*}$ 的面板 $*k*$，使得面板对 $(*i*, *k*)$ 和 $(*k*, *j*)$ 都满足前两个条件。

此时，![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c59da485d3a4e463f0157335ace916b7c377dcd8.png) 的 **水流量** 等于 $*min*(*r*_{*i*}, *r*_{*j*}) - *max*(*l*_{*i*}, *l*_{*j*})$，即它们的水平投影相交部分的长度。

Emuskald 决定在他的瀑布中，水将沿着一条从顶部到底部的路径流动。如果水流到某个面板（墙底除外），它将继续落到**恰好一个**更低的面板上。因此，瀑布中的总水流量定义为瀑布路径上相邻两个面板之间的水平投影相交长度的最小值。形式化地说：

1. 瀑布由一条面板路径组成 (![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/19e243d0761d715c71c322f6d06337878267eae8.png)）；
2. 瀑布的水流量是该路径中的最小水流量 (![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/19e243d0761d715c71c322f6d06337878267eae8.png)）。

为了建造一座真正壮观的瀑布，Emuskald 必须最大化这个水流量，但面板数量太多，使得规划工作十分困难。下面是一个 Emuskald 希望建造的瀑布示例：

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/4da5829cfd11950499f15e49228952c7f8b0ce83.png)

请帮助 Emuskald 维护自己的声誉，求出可能的最大水流量。

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含两个用空格分隔的整数 $*n*$ 和 $*t*$（$1 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}$，$2 ≤ *t* ≤ 10^{9}$），分别表示不包括顶部和底部面板在内的面板数量，以及墙的高度。接下来的 $*n*$ 行中，每行包含三个用空格分隔的整数 $*h*_{*i*}$、$*l*_{*i*}$ 和 $*r*_{*i*}$（$0 < *h*_{*i*} < *t*$，$- 10^{9} ≤ *l*_{*i*} < *r*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$），分别表示第 $*i*$ 个面板线段的高度、左端点和右端点。

保证任意两个线段都不共有点。

## 输出格式

输出一个整数，即所要求瀑布可能达到的最大水流量。

## 说明

第一个测试用例对应题目中的图片。
